You are fixing a bug in the Click repository checked out at /click (source in /click/src/click, tests in /click/tests). Do NOT touch any file other than /click/src/click/types.py (and you may create temporary scratch test files under /tmp only, never inside /click/tests).

GOAL: Make the behaviour of the Path type's symlink resolution correct, so that a test named `tests.test_types::test_symlink_resolution` would pass. The name describes the expected behaviour: `click.Path(resolve_path=True)` (and the `resolve_path` option) must resolve symlinks, i.e. it should behave like `os.path.realpath` (resolve symlinks in the path), not merely `os.path.abspath`. Look at `Path.convert` and the `resolve_path` handling in /click/src/click/types.py, compare it against the documented behaviour in /click/docs/parameters.rst (search for `resolve_path`) and the docstring of `click.Path`, and fix the discrepancy in the minimal way (the upstream fix makes resolve_path use realpath so symlinks are resolved). Do not change unrelated behaviour, do not edit any existing test file, and do not add new features.

VERIFY: run `cd /click && python -m pytest tests -q` and confirm there are no new failures (baseline is 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed). Also write your own scratch test in /tmp (e.g. /tmp/check_symlink.py) that creates a symlink with tempfile/os.symlink and asserts that click.Path(resolve_path=True).convert(...) returns the real (symlink-resolved) path, and run it with python. Report: the exact diff you made, the test results, and your confidence that a test named test_symlink_resolution passes.
